html:
The Albanian exodus began in 1990 and 1991, when the communist regime collapsed and tens of thousands of Albanians fled by sea to Italy and on foot to Greece. In August 1991 a single cargo ship, the Vlora, carried some 20,000 people into the port of Bari.

Emigration went on for decades. By the 2010s about a third of Albania's people lived abroad, mostly in Italy and Greece, adding to older communities such as the Arbëreshë of southern Italy. Money sent home became a main source of income, and empty villages spread across the highlands. The losses in the pyramid scheme collapse of 1997 sent another wave out. Emigration shrank the population of Albania and changed its towns and politics.
